en: In the *Devatāyoga* section of the *Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā* (Īnui’s edition):
"Thereafter, for the purpose of cultivating the three meditative absorptions (*samādhi*), the yoga of the deity (*devatāyoga*) is to be performed."
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by nature; I am pure by nature. Having performed the internal bath through the resolute conviction in selflessness.

Through the transformation of the syllable *HŪṂ* into a vajra, one should meditate on oneself as Vajrajvālānalārka—blue in color, with eight arms and four faces. With the two primary arms, he holds a vajra and a vajra-bell in the gesture of embracing Prajñā. With another pair of arms, he holds a sword and a noose with the threatening gesture (*tarjanī*). With another pair of arms, he holds a wheel and a *khaṭvāṅga*. With the final pair of arms, he holds a bow and an arrow. His principal face is black, the right white, the left red, and the rear yellow. Each face has three eyes.
One should meditate upon him adorned with ornaments of serpents, trampling the splendor of Nārāyaṇa in the pratyālīḍha posture, possessing a wrathful form, and embellished with all ornaments.

Then, having generated an eight-petaled lotus at the throat with the syllable *hrīḥ* and a white five-pronged vajra on the petal of the tongue-lotus with the syllable *hūṃ*, one should consecrate it with this [mantra].
Vajra-tongue.

With the syllable *A* on both hands, one should visualize two moon discs; above those, by means of two *HŪṂ* syllables, one should visualize two five-pronged vajras. One should then consider the fingers themselves to be needles and perform the destruction of obstacles and other such rites.
Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ vaṃ.
One should bind Krodhaterittarī.
Oṃ, seize, O Vajrasamaya, hūṃ vaṃ! Having placed the vajra-binding beneath [the feet], one should cover [it] with a mind full of wrath.
Firmly [pressed] with the vajra of the thumb, she is known as Krodhatara.
Then, one should receive the garland consecration.

Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ abhiṣiñca māṃ. For the vajra-binding, the two thumbs are joined and raised; one should hold it on the head, above the forehead, above the right ear, on the back, and above the left ear. This is the vajra-terettarī.
Oṃ tuṃ.

One should armor [the body] with the two-syllable armor-mantra. With both vajra-fists, one should perform the gesture of tying a knot at the heart; likewise on the back of the neck, again at the heart, between the breasts, again at the heart, and on the back of the neck. Having performed the gesture of tying a knot at the forehead, one should satisfy [the deity] at the head with the *samatāla* rhythm at the conclusion of the yoga of the cloth-consecration (*paṭābhiṣeka*).
Vajra tuṣya hoḥ!
Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ.
Placing the left vajra-fist at the heart and brandishing the vajra with the right hand, one should destroy all obstacles.
Then, with the pride of Vajrānala, one should perform the burning away of obstacles and so forth.

Oṃ vajrānala hana daha paca matha bhañja raṇa hūṃ phaṭ! Within the internal vajra-binding, with the thumb as the vajra and the raised fingers containing flames within their core—this is the *vajrānalasamayamudrā*.
Thereafter: "O Vajranetrī, bind all obstacles!"
Having formed the vajra-bandha and extended the two thumbs, one should place them upon the two eyes, the left and the right; this is the Vajramaitrī-samaya-mudrā.
Then, with the pride (*ahaṅkāra*) of Vajrarakṣā, one should consecrate [the ground] as consisting of vajras:
*oṃ vajra dṛḍho me bhava rakṣa sarvān svāhā*. Having placed the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*) with the arms extended upon the ground, this is the samaya-mudrā of Vajrarakṣā.
Thereafter, with the pride of Vajrabhairava, one should bind [the winds] upward.
Oṃ hulu 2 hūṃ phaṭ!
Having formed two vajra-fists, one should whirl them like a firebrand above the head and hold them at the forehead with the index fingers shaped like hooks. This is the Vajrabhairava Eye Mudrā.
In the same manner, one should bind it upwards with the pride of the Vajrayakṣa.
Oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ.
The Vajrayakṣa Samaya-mudrā consists of the vajra-añjali with both thumbs extended and both index fingers forming fangs.
Then, with the pride of being an Uṣṇīṣacakravartin, one should bind the eastern direction.
Oṃ drūṃ bandha hūṃ. Or: drūm.

Forming two vajra-fists with the little fingers linked together, one should turn the tips of the two index fingers into a needle-point and place them upon the crown of the head; this is the Vajroṣṇīṣa Samaya-mudrā.
Thereafter, one should bind all obstacles with the pride of being Vajrapāśa.
Oṃ vajrapāśa hrīḥ.
Having formed a knot with the arms by extending both vajra-fists, this is the vajrapāśa mudrā.
Then, with the pride of being the Vajrayaṣṭi, one should bind the western direction.
Oṃ, O Vajra-bannered one, O winged one, roar!

The *samaya-mudrā* of Vajrapatāka is formed by the *vajra-bandha*, with the two thumbs placed in the lap-pointing position (*paryaṅkasūcī*) and the tips of the little fingers joined and spread apart at the edge of the cloth.
Then, with the pride of Vajrakalyāṇa, one should perform the devouring of obstacles and bind the northern direction.
Hrīḥ Vajrakāli maṭ!
Having firmly placed the Vajrayakṣa mudrā at the mouth, it is the Vajrakālī samaya mudrā.
With the pride of the Vajraśikhara, one should bind the southern direction.
Oṃ vajraśikhara ruṭ maṭ.
Having made the gesture of lifting up a mountain with both vajra-fists, one should strike away the obstacles in the southern direction. This is the Vajraśikhara mudrā.
Then, with the ego-identification of Vajrakarma, one should establish the vajra enclosure.
Oṃ Vajrakarma.

Having formed two vajra-fists with the two little fingers linked back-to-back, one should raise the two middle fingers and index fingers and conceal them with the two thumbs and ring fingers; this is the enclosure mudrā of Vajrakarma.
Thereafter, one should construct the inner enclosure by means of the yoga of Vajra-hūṃkāra.
Oṃ, by means of Vajrahūṃkāra, hūṃ!
By contracting the two middle fingers with the Vajrakarmamudrā, it becomes the Trailokyavijayamudrā.
Then, with the pride of Vajrasandhi, one should bestow the vajra-cage.
Oṃ vajrabandha vaṃ.
Having extended [the fingers] upward with a graceful play by means of the vajra-bind, it is the pañjara-mudrā.
Furthermore, one should purify the components of the offering with the pride of Vajrānala, joined with its corresponding mudrā.
Oṃ vajrānala, strike, burn, cook, churn, shatter, roar, hūṃ phaṭ!
Then, with the Vajrayakṣa mudrā, there is the consecration of the conch.
Oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ.
Furthermore, one should perform the consecration of the conch using the Vajrarakṣa mudrā.
Oṃ vajrarakṣa aḥ.
Furthermore, by means of the Vajraśikhara mudrā, there is the consecration of the conch.
Oṃ vajraśikhara ruṭ maṭ.
Thus ends the triad of conchs.
Again, having empowered the three conch shells with the Vajrasattva Samaya-mudrā and the Vairocana Samaya-mudrā, [recite]:
Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ.
Oṃ vajradhātu hūṃ.
One should sprinkle all the components of the worship with that water from the conch.
Oṃ vajrarakṣa hūṃ.
with this mantra.
Oṃ vajrapuṣpe hūṃ.
The flower.
Oṃ vajradhūpe hūṃ.
Incense.
Oṃ vajrāloke hūṃ.
The island.
Oṃ vajragandhe hūṃ.
Fragrance.
Oṃ vajranaivedye hūṃ.
Having consecrated the food offering with its respective mudrā.
Oṃ, the syllable A is the gateway to all phenomena because they are primordially unarisen; Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ.
With the sword mudrā, [offer] the bali; with the vajra-bind, the raising of the sword, the gesture of the sword.
One should consecrate the other limbs of worship with the Vajrasattva mudrā:
Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrāsani hūṃ.
The posture.
Thus ends the protection wheel.
Immediately following that, one should manifest the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu in front by means of the vajra-cause action-seal (karmamudrā).
Oṃ vajracakre hūṃ.

Having formed the two vajra-fists, with the tips of the two outer fingers joined in the vajra-bind, this is known as the Vajracakra, which accomplishes all maṇḍalas. By revolving this [mudrā] clockwise in all directions, the manifestation of all maṇḍalas occurs. Looking at this very mudrā in one's mouth, one should recite [the mantra] eight times; one thereby becomes entered into all maṇḍalas.

There, having seen the mandala as if it were directly before one's eyes, one should perform the offering of water (argha) and so forth, after having drawn [the deities] in with the vajra-hook and other implements, caused them to enter, bound them, and brought them under control.
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa jaḥ!
Oṃ vajrapāśa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ.
Oṃ vajrāveśa hoḥ!
Then, one should offer the arghya with the arghya-mudrā.
Oṃ, for the sake of the most excellent offering to the Vajradhātu, accept it! Svāhā!
In three ways.
Oṃ, for the supreme honor of the Vajradhātu, accept this water for the feet; svāhā!
The washing of the feet for the water for the guests.
Oṃ, for the excellent service of the Vajradhātu, accept this water for rinsing the mouth; svāhā!
The ritual sipping of water.
Oṃ vajrarakṣa hūṃ.
Sprinkling.
Then, one should perform the placement of flowers upon the mandala.
Oṃ vajradhātu hūṃ.
In the middle.
Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ.
In the east.
Oṃ vajraratna trāṃ.
In the south.
Oṃ dharmavajra hrīḥ.
In the west.
Oṃ karmavajra aḥ.
In the north.
Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ.
[Recite this] in the presence of Akṣobhya.
Oṃ Vajrarāja Jaḥ!
[This is] to the right of Akṣobhya.
Oṃ vajrarāga hoḥ.
To the left of Akṣobhya.
Oṃ Vajrasādhu saḥ!
On the back of Akṣobhya.
Oṃ vajraratna oṃ.
Oṃ vajrateja āṃ.
Oṃ Vajraketu Trāṃ.
Oṃ vajrahāsa hāṃ.
The [mandala] of Ratnasambhava is like that of Akṣobhya.
Oṃ Vajradharma Hrīḥ.
Oṃ vajratīkṣṇa dhaṃ.
Oṃ vajrahetu maṃ.
Oṃ vajrabhāṣa raṃ.
As before, [this applies] to Amitābha.
Oṃ vajrakarma kaṃ.
Oṃ vajrarakṣa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrasandhi vaṃ.
As before, this applies to Amoghasiddhi.
Thus, these [are placed] within the womb-cavity.
Oṃ vajralāsye hūṃ.
Oṃ vajramāle hūṃ.
Oṃ vajragīte hrīḥ.
Oṃ vajranṛtye aḥ.
Outside, in the four corners of the mandalas beginning with the southeast (āgneya), etc.
In the four corners of the outer maṇḍala are the offerings beginning with incense (dhūpa).
Oṃ vajradhūpe hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrapuṣpe trāṃ.
Oṃ vajraloke hrīḥ.
Oṃ vajragandhe aḥ.
Then, on both sides of the gates starting from the east, etc.
Oṃ, for the seizing of Maitreya, svāhā!
Oṃ, to Amoghadarśin, hūṃ!
Oṃ, you who abandon all lower realms, you who purify all lower realms, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O you whose mind dispels all sorrow and darkness, hūṃ!
In the east.
Oṃ, to Gandhahastin, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Śūraṅgama, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O you who are in the sky, whose eyes are the sky, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Jñānaketu, possessor of wisdom, hūṃ!
In the south.
Oṃ, O you of nectar-like radiance, O possessor of nectar, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Moon, you who abide in the moon, you who gaze upon the moon, svāhā!
Oṃ, O Auspicious One, O Guardian of the Auspicious, hūṃ!
Oṃ, O Jvālinī, O Mahājvālinī, hūṃ!
In the west.
Oṃ vajragarbhe hūṃ.
Oṃ, to the imperishable, hūṃ, purifier of imperishable karmic obscurations, svāhā!
Oṃ, to Pratibhānakūṭa, svāhā!
Oṃ Samantabhadre hūṃ.
In the north.
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa jaḥ!
Oṃ vajrapāśa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ.
Oṃ vajrāveśa hoḥ!
At the eastern gate and so forth.
Once again, before Vairocana.
Oṃ satvavajrī hūṃ.
In the south.
Oṃ Ratnavajrī Trāṃ.
In the west.
Oṃ Dharmavajrī Hrīḥ!
In the north.
Oṃ karmavajrī aḥ.
Thus is the sequential placement of the flowers.
Then, having worshipped with flowers and other offerings;
Oṃ āḥ vajrapuṣpe hūṃ.
Oṃ āḥ vajradhūpe hūṃ.
Oṃ āḥ vajrāloke hūṃ.
Oṃ āḥ vajragandhe hūṃ.
Oṃ vajranaivedye hūṃ.
Then, one should form the eight mudrās, beginning with the lāsya.
Oṃ, to the one worthy of worship through the perfection of generosity arising from the great vajra of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Oṃ, to the one worthy of worship through the perfection of ethical discipline arising from all the Tathāgatas, Trāṃ!
Oṃ, to the one worthy of worship through the perfection of patience arising from all the Tathāgatas, Hrīḥ!
Oṃ! To the one worthy of worship through the perfection of great heroism arising from all the Tathāgatas: Aḥ!
Oṃ, arising from all the Tathāgatas, purifier of all miserable rebirths, O Puṣpāvalokinī, worthy of worship through the Perfection of Wisdom, hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, arising from all Tathāgatas, purifier of all lower realms, burn, burn! Incense! Incense! O you who are worthy of worship through the perfection of meditative concentration! Trāṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, purifier of all miserable rebirths of all Tathāgatas, maker of the light of wisdom, worthy of worship through the perfection of aspiration, hrīḥ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, O you who destroy the odor of all the evil destinies of all Tathāgatas, Vajra-fragrance, worthy of worship through the perfection of skillful means! Aḥ Hūṃ Phaṭ!
Having fully worshipped these with the aforementioned karmamudrā.
Then, one should ring the bell.
From this mountain, we have come to those whose nature is the essence of the Dharma.
They are compassionate by nature and are the removers of suffering in the world.
Bestowers of the accomplishment of all qualities without exception.
They possess the supreme and foremost Dharma, which is unshakable and peerless.
In the sky, nothing comparable has been found.
Even toward a mere atom or speck of a fraction of their virtues, which are themselves boundless.
O bestower of the supreme accomplishment of the realm of existence and non-existence!
Among those who are beyond comparison and possess universal accomplishment.
Constantly stainless, it arises from the impetus of compassion.
The fulfillment of one's vow is the nature of non-cessation.
She is intent on accomplishing the welfare of the world and is skilled in counsel.
It shines eternally for those whose nature is great compassion.
Non-ceasing, the practice of compassion, and immovability.
She proceeds, bestowing the supreme accomplishment of the three worlds.
They have reached a state perfectly established amidst the immeasurable and the immeasurably great.
Even for those who have gone to a happy rebirth, oh, how wonderful is the nature of the Dharma!
May they, who grant the supreme siddhi of the three samayas, bestow it upon me.
The state of granting boons has reached the highest excellence; it is the constant course.
They bestow all the supreme accomplishments of the three worlds.
The Protectors have gone to the three realms and are unobstructed.
Thus one should praise with this offering of hymns.
Then, one should prostrate with the five-pointed salutation (*pañcamandalaka*): in the eastern direction, with the body together with the vajra-añjali gesture.
Oṃ, with a prostration of the body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas, I perform the vajra-salutation.
Oṃ, I offer myself for the service and worship of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas, please empower me!
On the right, one should hold the vajra-añjali at the heart, touching the ground with the forehead, and say:
"Oṃ, I offer myself for the consecration of worship to all Tathāgatas;
Oṃ, consecrate me with the vajra-jewel of all Tathāgatas."
Placing the vajra-añjali at the head while touching the ground with the mouth in the west;
Oṃ, I offer myself for the sake of initiating the worship of all Tathāgatas;
Oṃ, initiate me into the Vajra-dharma of all Tathāgatas!
Then, having placed his kneecaps upon the ground and joined his palms at his heart, he should confess his misdeeds.

May all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the ten directions, and all the deities of the mudrās, mantras, and vidyās residing within the Tathāgata, Vajra, Ratna, Padma, and Karma families, attend to me! I, [name], in the presence of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the ten directions, and in the presence of all the deities of the mudrās, mantras, and vidyās residing within the Tathāgata, Vajra, Ratna, Padma, and Karma families, confess every sin.

In detail, throughout the ten directions, I rejoice in all the merit of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present; of the Pratyekabuddhas and Noble Śrāvakas who have correctly entered the path; and of all classes of sentient beings who are correctly practicing the way. To all the Blessed Buddhas in the ten directions who have not yet set in motion the Wheel of Dharma, I entreat them to turn the Wheel of Dharma.
To all the Blessed Buddhas in the ten directions who desire to enter final Nirvāṇa, I beseech them not to pass into final Nirvāṇa.
Thus ends the confession of misdeeds and so forth.
Then, one should perform twenty offerings accompanied by mantras and mudrās.
Then, having formed the flower-samayamudrā, one should speak as follows:
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like clouds of flower offerings of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Having formed the samaya-mudrā of incense, one should speak thus:
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of incense offerings of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Having bound the lamp-samaya-mudrā, one should speak as follows:
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of light-offering of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Thus, with the fragrance-samaya-mudrā.
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of fragrance-offerings of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Having formed a jeweled gesture of salutation with joined palms, one should speak as follows.
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings consisting of the jewel ornaments of the factors of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Having performed the dramatic representation of laughter, one should speak as follows.
Oṃ, to the great assembly that fills the oceans of clouds of unsurpassed offerings consisting of the laughter, dance, pleasure, play, and bliss of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Having formed the mudrā of the gift of clothing, one should speak as follows:
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings consisting of the garments and ornaments of the awakening factors of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Having bound the Vajrasattva-karmamudrā, one should speak as follows:
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like clouds of vajra worship of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Having formed the *lāsyā-karmamudrā*, one should speak as follows:
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings of the perfection of generosity arising from the great vajra of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
One should speak with the mudrā of the garland-making rite.
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings of the perfection of ethical discipline that brings about the unsurpassed enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
With the Gītā-karma-mudrā.
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings for the perfection of patience that awakens to the unexcelled Dharma of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
By means of the dance-action mudrā.
Oṃ, to the great assembly of spreading clouds and oceans of offerings of the unsurpassed perfection of vigor through the renunciation of the saṃsāra of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
With the mudrā of the incense ritual.
Oṃ! At the moment of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings consisting of the perfection of meditative concentration, which is the dwelling in the unsurpassed bliss of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
With the flower-action mudrā.
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings to the Great Perfection of Wisdom, which cuts through the supreme afflictions of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
By means of the lamp-offering mudrā.
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings of the great vow-perfection of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
By means of the fragrance-action mudrā.

Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings of the vajra-fragrance, the skillful means of the perfection of fragrance that destroys the stench of the miserable realms of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Placing his joined palms in salutation upon his head, he should speak as follows:
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings consisting of the emanation of the bodies of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Having slightly opened the vajrāñjali at the mouth, one should speak thus:
Oṃ, at the moment of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings consisting of the vocal emanations of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Having formed the hollowed-añjali gesture at the heart, one should speak as follows:
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings consisting of the surrendering of the minds of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive ocean-like cloud of offerings that presents the secrets of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
By means of the gesture of embracing.
Having thus worshiped all the Tathāgatas with these twenty kinds of offerings, one should offer oneself.
I offer myself to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas at all times and for all eternity; may you, the compassionate Lords, accept me and grant me the accomplishment of the Great Samaya.

Furthermore, that root of merit should be made common to all sentient beings. By this root of merit, may all sentient beings be freed from all mundane and supramundane misfortunes, and endowed with all mundane and supramundane prosperities; together with happiness and together with joy, may they become Buddhas, the supreme among men.
And by this wholesome deed, may I become a Buddha in this world before long.
"Teach the Dharma for the sake of the world; may I liberate sentient beings who are oppressed by manifold sufferings. Thus one should dedicate [the merit] toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Thus ends the generation of the thought of awakening.
I generate the supreme, unsurpassed mind of awakening (bodhicitta),
just as the Protectors of the three times have made their firm resolve for perfect enlightenment.
I firmly undertake the threefold training in ethical discipline, the gathering of virtuous qualities, and the ethical discipline of acting for the benefit of sentient beings.
The Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha—the unsurpassed, supreme Triple Gem.
From this day forward, I shall take up the vow born of the yoga of the Buddha;
I truly accept the vajra, the bell, and the mudrā.
And I shall accept a master within the exalted assembly of the Great Vajra Family.
I shall bestow the fourfold gift six times every day,
within the yoga of the Great Jewel Family and during the delightful samaya.
I accept the True Dharma— outer and secret, belonging to the three vehicles—
within the pure Mahāpadma family, which gives rise to great awakening;
I accept the vow fully endowed with all [precepts] according to reality.
One should perform the rite of worship according to one's ability within the great accumulation of ritual actions.
I generate the supreme, unsurpassed bodhicitta;
I have undertaken the complete vow for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings.
I shall cause those who have not crossed over to cross; I shall liberate those who are not yet liberated.
I shall bring comfort to beings who have not yet found comfort, and I shall establish them in final liberation.
Thus concludes the undertaking of the vows.
Thus ends the yoga of beginningless accomplishment.

Immediately thereafter, through the application of reflected images and so forth, preceded by the binding of mudrās, one should consecrate everything, having first performed the *kamalāvarta* [mudrā].
Oṃ, all phenomena are mutually interpenetrating; [this is] the joined palms in the hollowed gesture.
Oṃ, all phenomena are mutually interpenetrated;
[this is] the vajra-añjali.
Oṃ, all phenomena have entered utterly [into the state of non-duality]; vajra-bind, vaṃ!
Oṃ vajrabandha traṭ.
One should burst the triple vajra-bind at the heart. This is the release of the vajra-bind.
Having bound the samaya-mudrā of the vajra-entrance, one should visualize the primordial vajra at the heart by means of the syllable A.
Oṃ! Abide, O Vajra; be firm for me, be eternal for me; empower my heart and grant me all accomplishments! Hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ!
Oṃ vajrāveśa aḥ!
Oṃ, all phenomena are mutually interpenetrating;
Oṃ Vajramuṣṭi Vaṃ.
One should hold the vajra-fist separately in each heart.
Thereafter, having formed the vajra-bind, from between the two vajra-mudrās—
Once it has arisen, one should cast it upward in an instant; this is the supreme upward-throwing technique.
Oṃ, vajra-samaya of the extraction and purification of all sins, hūṃ phaṭ!
The extraction of evil.

Reciting: "Oṃ Vajrapāṇi, shatter all bonds of the lower realms! Liberate all sentient beings from all states of rebirth in the lower realms! O vajra-samaya of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ traṭ!"—thus speaking, one should shatter evil in three ways.
Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the two middle fingers joined at their tips and the fourth fingers attached to the tips of the others, one shatters evil in an instant.
Having bound the Vairocana-samaya-mudrā, one should recite the mantra three times.
Oṃ vajra muḥ:
the dismissal of evil.
In this way, one becomes a performer who casts down all mudrās; and by means of this, the yogin becomes like a bodhisattva who has emerged after three incalculable eons.
Then, mentally uttering "Vajrasattva" in the center of the vajra within one's own heart, one should meditate on the selflessness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmanairātmya*).

With this [syllable] accompanied by the sixteen vowels, one should visualize a moon mandala; then, with the consonants beginning with *ka*, a second moon mandala; and upon that, a white five-pronged vajra with rays of light as its emblem, together with the heart-mantra. For others, however, having placed their respective mudrās, mantras, and emblems in the center of the vajra-born [mandala], they should cultivate the pride of the mudrā. Having bound the Great Vajra Universal Mudrā (*vajrasarvamahāmudrā*), one should speak thus:
I am Vajra; I am Vajra; I am Ratna.
I am Padma;
I am Viśvavajra.
I am the vajra;
I am the hook;
I am the arrow.
I am contentment;
I am the jewel;
I am the sun.
I am Ketu; I am Smiti;
I am Padma.
I am Khaḍga; I am Cakra; I am Jihva.
I am Karmāha; I am Varmmāha; I am Daṃṣṭra.
I am the Fist.
I am the double-vajra;
I am the jewel-garland;
I am the lute.
I am the dancer with hands like tender shoots; I am incense;
I am flowers.
I am the lamp; I am the fragrance.
I am the goad; I am the noose; I am the chain.
I am Ghaṇṭa.
While reciting the mantra of one's own heart, having caused [the deities] to enter the vajra-realms of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, one should contemplate their respective mudrās.
In this regard, the mudrā is as follows:
"I am Vajradhātu;
I am Vajrasattva."
I am Ratnavajra;
I am Padmavajra;
I am Viśvavajra.
I am Vajrasattva;
I am Vajrarāja;
I am Vajrarāga.
I am Vajrasādhu;
I am Vajragarbha;
I am Vajraprabha.
I am Vajrayaṣṭi;
I am Vajraprīti;
I am Vajranetra.
I am Vajrabuddhi;
I am Vajramaṇḍa;
I am Vajravāc.
I am Vajrakarman;
I am Vajravīrya; I am Vajracaṇḍa.
I am Vajramuṣṭi.
I am Vajralāsyā;
I am Vajramālā;
I am Vajragītā.
I am Vajranṛtyā; I am Vajradhūpā;
I am Vajrapuṣpā.
I am Vajradīpā;
I am Vajragandhā.
I am Vajrāṅkuśa;
I am Vajrapāśa;
I am Vajrasphoṭa.
I am the vajra-possessor.
Having said this, one should contemplate the form of one's own respective deity within one's own heart.
Having done this, one should meditate upon the complete Vajradhātu-maṇḍala within one's own heart.
Having visualized oneself in the form of Vajrasattva.
Having bound the Vajrasattva-samaya-mudrā, one should speak thus:
"I am the pledge;
I am the pledge; I am the pledge-being.
With that very mudrā, one should empower [the body] at the heart, the ūrṇā, the throat, and the crown of the head.
"Empower me as the Samayasattva!
Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ!
Having uttered this, one should brandish the vajra.
Again, having radiated vajra-rays from the moon in one’s own heart, one should emanate and behold the Vajradhātu-maṇḍala in the sky by means of the vajra-cause karma-mudrā.
By means of the Vajrasattva Samaya-mudrā: "You are the samaya; I am the samaya."
Having bound the samaya-mudrā of vajrāveśa, one should recite "tiṣṭha vajra" and so forth three times, as before.

One should visualize the two mandalas as having become one. Having made oneself into a subtle form in space, and having formed the sattvavajrī mudrā and taken a flower garland, one should enter the mandala.
Thus, this disciple has been initiated by me into the delightful maṇḍala;
may there be merit, and likewise may the lineage of the deities be established.

Whatever kind of accomplishment he may attain, in whatever lineage he is a vessel, and whatever the power of his merit may be—may such [attainment] be his within this mandala. Accept it, O Vajra! Hoḥ!
The scattering of flowers.
Then, one should receive the garland consecration.
Oṃ, O child of great power, please accept this;
[this is] the flower consecration.
Having bound the Satvavajrī [mudrā], one should open the eyes.
Oṃ! Vajrasattva himself, intent today upon opening your eyes, opens for you the unsurpassed vajra-eye with the vajra-eye.
O Vajra, behold!
This is the opening of the eyes.
Then he should show the mandala, beginning with Vajrāṅkuśa and ending with the Blessed One Vairocana.
Then, having placed the vajra upon his head and consecrated him with the water from the flask held by Satvavajrī and the others, [the master says]:
"Oṃ vajrābhiṣiñca māṃ. This is the water consecration (udakābhiṣeka).
Then, one should receive the crown and ribbon consecration of the five Buddhas.
Oṃ Vajradhātvīśvarī hūṃ Vajriṇī, confer the empowerment upon me!

On the crown of the head, one should visualize Vairocana, white in color, abiding in the Bodhyagrī mudrā. Having formed the vajrāñjali, with the two thumbs placed in the cross-legged posture and their tips bent, and with the middle fingers and the topmost parts held level—this is known as Vajradhātvīśvarī.
*Oṃ vajravajriṇi hūṃ abhiṣiñca māṃ*.
Above the forehead is Akṣobhya, blue in color, in the earth-touching mudrā; that same middle finger, however, when it is a vajra, is known as Vajravajriṇī.
Oṃ ratnavajriṇi hūṃ, empower me!
Above the right ear is yellow Ratnasambhava, in the boon-granting (*varada*) mudrā; having formed jewels with the two middle fingers, she is known as Ratnavajrī.
*Oṃ dharmavajriṇi hūṃ abhiṣiñca māṃ*.
On the back of the head is red Amitābha, in the meditative concentration (*samādhi*) mudrā; by this [mudrā] formed with the middle, ring, and little fingers like a lotus, she is known as Dharmavajrī.
Oṃ karmavajriṇi hūṃ, consecrate me!
Above the left ear is Amoghasiddhi, who is the seal of action (*karmamudrā*). With fingers extended, she is known as Karmavajrī.
Thus ends the consecration with pearls.
Thereafter, one should don the armor as before and perform the equalizing rhythmic clapping.
Then one should receive the vajra initiation, holding the vajra at the heart.
"Today you have been consecrated by the Buddhas through the vajra-consecration.
Take this, which is the state of all Buddhas, the vajra for the sake of perfect accomplishment.
Thus is the vajra-consecration.
One should hold the vajra and the vajra-bell with pride.
Oṃ, I consecrate you as the Vajra Lord; remain firm, O Vajra, for you are the Samaya.
Thus concludes the initiation of the knots.
One should hold the vajra and the vajra-bell at the head.
Oṃ, Vajrasattva, I consecrate you with the vajra-name consecration.
He is the glorious, eternal Tathāgata named Vajra; Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ.
Thus is the name-consecration.
Then, having taken up the vajra and holding the vajra and vajra-bell, he should form the great mudrā of Vajrasattva.
This is that state of all-buddhahood, which resides in the hand of Vajrasattva;
you too must always uphold it, O Vajrapāṇi of firm vows.
Thus is the vajra-vow.
Oṃ, O Vajra-samaya of the accomplishment of all Tathāgatas, abide! I cause you, O Vajrasattva, to hold [this]; hi hi hi hi hūṃ!
Thus is the commitment of the bell.

Having thus performed the self-consecration (*svādhiṣṭhāna*), one should practice the accomplishment. First of all, in that regard, one should contemplate one’s own heart as a moon-maṇḍala, [with the seed-syllable] unified within it.
Then, [one should place it] upon one's own body.
*Samaya āḥ*. While reciting [the mantra], one should visualize a moon mandala.
Vajrasattva, Aḥ;
again, the moon;
by means of the syllable Hūṃ, the vajra.
"I am Vajra. Through that transformation, one should meditate upon oneself as Vajrasattva, white in color, and cultivate the pride of being him.
I am Vajrasattva.
Having beheld the great body of Vajrasattva, one should bind the Mahāmudrā.
Then, one should meditate upon the body mandala.
Oṃ vajrasattva hūṃ; one should recite this.
One should visualize the lunar disk in twenty-eight locations.
In this regard, the following is the seed:
Vajrasattva Āḥ.
Vajrarāja aḥ.
Vajrarāga aḥ.
Vajrasādhu aḥ!
Vajraratna aḥ.
Vajra-Tejas ĀḤ.
Vajraketu āḥ.
Vajrahāsa Aḥ!
Vajradharma Āḥ.
Vajratīkṣṇa, Aḥ!
Vajra-hetu aḥ.
Vajra-speech: Aḥ!
Vajrakarma Āḥ.
Vajrarakṣa aḥ.
Vajrayakṣa Aḥ!
Vajra-joint: Aḥ.
Vajralāsye aḥ.
Vajramāle aḥ.
Aḥ in the Vajra Song.
Aḥ for the vajra dance.
Vajradhūpe aḥ.
Vajrapuṣpe aḥ.
In the Vajrāloka: Aḥ.
Vajragandhe aḥ.
Vajrāṅkuśa, Aḥ!
Vajrapāśa aḥ.
Vajrasphoṭa: AḤ.
Vajrāveśa, aḥ!
One should see a sword above it.
One should recite from "I am Vajra" up to "I am Ghaṇṭa."
Through the transformation of the seed-syllable and the emblem, one should meditate upon the form of the deity.
"The seed-syllable;
'I am Vajrasattva'—up to this point, one should recite: 'I am the Vajra-encasement.'"
In this regard, this is the station of the deity.
In the heart is white Vajrasattva.
To the right of Vajrasattva is yellow Vajrarāja;
to the left is red Vajrarāga;
and at the back is emerald-colored Vajrasādhu.
On the forehead is a yellow vajra-jewel.
Upon the head and back is the vajra-splendor, radiant as the sun.
On the two shoulders is Vajraketu, with the luster of the sky;
on the row of teeth is Vajrahāsa, white as a lotus stalk;
and on the throat is Vajradharma, white and red.
Between the breasts is Vajratīkṣṇa, dark blue like the sky;
at the navel is Vajrahetu, golden yellow;
on the tongue is Vajrabhāṣa, resembling copper.
Upon the crown of the head is the multicolored Vajrakarma.
The two shoulders have diamond protection, golden in appearance.
On the face is black Vajrayakṣa;
on the hips is yellow Vajrasandhi.
On the left side of Vajrasattva is Lāsyā, white;
on the left side of Ratna is Mālā, yellow;
on the left side of Dharma is Gītā, red.
Dancing in the left [hand] of the universe, she is of universal color;
for the practitioner, she is white incense within the bladder.
Puṣpā is yellow at the head;
Dīpā is red at the eyes;
Gandhā is of variegated colors between the breasts.
On the right thigh is the white Vajrāṅkuśa;
on the left thigh is the black Vajrapāśa;
and on the right shank is the white Vajrasphoṭa.
On the left calf, one visualizes the multicolored Vajrāveśa;
having bound their respective great mudrās, one instantly manifests this form within one's own body as the deity in twenty-eight locations.
Thus is the pride of the seed-syllable, the emblem, and the deity.
Thereafter, as before, having emanated a mandala in space by means of the vajra-cause action-seal (karmamudrā) from the vajra-rays emerging from the heart, one should proceed.
Oṃ vajracakre hūṃ.
Having formed the assembly mudrā upon one's own body and the bodies of Vajrasattva and the others, one should speak as follows:
Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ.
By means of the mind and through the correct application, one should cause all Buddhas to enter.
With the two arms in the vajra-bind, through the release of the vajra-clap,
one whose self is the yoga of Śrī Vajrasattva should assemble all the Buddhas.

Success is achieved with the left-hand snap-clap (*vajrācchaṭaka*) and the equal clap (*samatāla*); by the right hand, however, both types of claps are declared. Thus is the *vajrācchaṭakasamāja-mudrā*.

Then, having drawn [the deity] in with the vajra-hook and other implements, having caused entry, bound, and brought under control, and having worshipped with the outer offerings such as the argha and so forth, one should show the samāja.
Oṃ vajradhātu dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrasattva dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ ratnavajra dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ! O Dharma-vajra, you who perceive the visible world! Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ karmavajra dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ Vajrasattva! You who are visible, jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrarāja dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrarāga dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrasādhu! O visible one, jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajraratna dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajrateja dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ Vajraketu! Behold! Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrahāsa dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajradharma dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajratīkṣṇa dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajrahetu dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrabhāṣa dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrakarma dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrarakṣa dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrayakṣa dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrasandhi dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajralāsye! O visible one, jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajramāle dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajragīte! O visible one, jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajranṛtye dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajradhūpe dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajrapuṣpe dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajrāloke dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ; you are the pledge, I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajragandhe dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.

Oṃ! O you who are pure in all conditioned phenomena, whose nature is the reality of the sky, arisen from the expanse of space, pure by intrinsic nature, surrounded by the Great Vehicle! Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ vajrapāśa dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the commitment; I am the commitment.
Oṃ vajrasphoṭa dṛśya jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the pledge; I am the pledge.
Oṃ! O you who are the descent of the supreme [power], visible one! Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! You are the samaya; I am the samaya.
Oṃ, to the Great Yogīśvara of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
One should recite it three times, or [recite] each [verse] individually.
And all the samaya-mudrās should be employed by producing a white five-pronged vajra with the syllable *hūṃ* in one's own heart.
In this regard, these are the characteristics of the mudrās:
All samaya-mudrās, however, arise from the vajra-binding.
I shall now explain their binding, the unsurpassed Vajrabandha.
Having made the *sattvavajrī* firm, with the middle fingers raised and joined like a sprout,
and with the tips of the middle fingers contracted inward, this second [mudrā] is described by the Buddhas.
The middle finger and thumb form the jewel; the middle fingers are contracted like a lotus.
The fifth is the Buddha-mudrā, likewise with the [thumb] slightly bent upward.
Now, I shall further explain another [mantra] belonging indeed to the Tathāgata family.
Upon a moon formed by both hands, with the middle fingers excluded.
The vajra of both the Sattva and the Vajra [families] is indeed joined with an extremely long finger-tip.
She who possesses the supreme goad; she who possesses the supreme union; she who bestows the cry of "Well done! (Sādhukāra).
This indeed is the host of mudrās for the accomplishment of the four Vajrasattvas.
The form of Ratnavajra arises from the joining of the faces of the threatening fingers.
That same [middle finger] is extended along with the middle and little fingers.
The banner mudrā (patākā), however, is formed by joining the middle fingers with the little fingers.
And she herself, standing in the place of laughter, is likewise transformed.
The thumb is extended and held level, while the index finger is bent.
That very same Vajrakośā is joined with the opening of the central face.
That same [state] is the equalized Ākanisthā, designated as the wheel.
But when released from the bound thumb, it arises with the mouth extended.
The action-vajrī is formed by joining the tips of the little finger and the thumb together.
That very same [mudrā], when well-extended and placed in the heart, is indeed the Samāgrā.
The tip of the little finger is bent at its nail and released from the joint.
One should press the two thumbs against the space between the little fingers with the tips of the hands clenched together.
In the heart, however, [the mudrā] with the thumbs level is Suprasāntā Mālinī.
When emerging from the mouth at the tips of the joined palms, they form a hollowed cup above the head of one who is dancing.
The vajrabandha [mudrā] is formed by placing the hands downward; the svāñjali is formed by raising them upward.
And there is pressure with the fingers joined together; [this is done] by means of a well-applied ointment.

Having placed the left *tathāgata-muṣṭi* face upwards, one should extend the little finger of the right hand starting from the index finger and thumb, and then form the hollowed *añjali*; these are the *samaya-mudrās* of Maitreya and the others.
The contraction of one index finger, with the two thumbs bound together in a knot.
The thumbs are bound at their tips; the tips of the vajra-fists are joined together.
Thus ends the description of the samaya-mudrās.
Immediately after that, having bound the Vairocana Mahāmudrā, one should place the Dharmamudrā upon the tongues of the Tathāgatas previously purified.
O Vajra Wisdom,
you are the commitment;
bring [it] forth!
Oh, what bliss!
Excellent, excellent! What great majesty!
The illumination of form,
the attainment of the goal: ha ha hūṃ he.
O you who accomplish all things, O you who cut through suffering,
O awakening of the Buddhas!
The echo is mastery and fearlessness.
O devourer of enemies,
bestower of all accomplishments, great delight!
In the beauty of form, in the pleasure of hearing, and in all worship.
O most radiant one, at the arrival of the fruit that brings delight!
Sugandhāgri oṃ, O nature of phenomena that is completely pure of all conditioned things, arisen like the sky, pure by its own nature, surrounded by the Great Vehicle, svāhā!
Āyāni jaḥ āhi hūṃ hūṃ he sphoṭa vaṃ.
The bell is "Aḥ Aḥ," the Dharma-mudrā.

Then one should bind the action-seal (karmamudrā). Having visualized a double-vajra (viśvavajra) at one's own heart by means of the syllable *A*, and having formed two vajra-fists, one who is composed should separate them into two.
Thereafter, the binding of the two vajra-mudrās will be explained.
The characteristics of the vajra-fist.
Oṃ vajradhātu hūṃ.
Grasping the left vajra-finger with the right hand raised up.
This mudrā named Bodhyagrī bestows the awakening of a Buddha.
Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ. With the left fist in the manner of holding the corner of a robe, one should place it at the heart; with the right hand, one should perform the earth-touching gesture.
Oṃ ratnavajra trāṃ. With this very [mantra], perform the gesture of granting boons with the right hand.
Oṃ dharmavajra hrīḥ!
The pinnacle of meditative concentration.
Oṃ karmavajra aḥ.
The left hand holds a handful of robes, and the right hand makes the gesture of granting fearlessness.
Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ.
Exalting with pride.
Oṃ vajrarāja jaḥ.
With two [hands], she is established in the act of grasping a hook.
Oṃ vajrarāga hoḥ.
And by means of the application of striking with arrows.
Oṃ vajrasādhu saḥ.
He dwells in the heart of those who offer words of praise.
Oṃ vajraratna oṃ.
In the consecration, however, there are two vajras.
Oṃ vajrateja āḥ.
The visualization of the sun in the heart.
Oṃ Vajraketu Trāṃ; and Vāmasthābāhudaṇḍā.
Oṃ vajrahāsa hāḥ!
In that way, his [face] was turned around.
Oṃ Vajradharma Hrīḥ.
Blossoming to the left and to the right.
Oṃ vajratīkṣṇa dhaṃ.
On the left side of the heart is Khaḍgadhāriṇī.
Oṃ vajrahetu maṃ!
[This is] the whirling of a firebrand.
Oṃ vajrabhāṣa raṃ. She arises from the two vajras at the mouth.
Oṃ vajrakarma kaṃ.
She stands upon the uṣṇīṣa, free from the whirling of the vajra dance, like a pigeon.
Oṃ vajrarakṣa hūṃ.
The tips of the fangs are like those of the youngest [tusk].
Oṃ vajramuṣṭi vaṃ. [This is] the pressing together of the two fists.
Oṃ vajralāsye hūṃ!
One should bow with the application of vajra-arrogance, with the body trembling from one's inner disposition.
Oṃ vajramāle trāṃ.
The Garland Composition.
Oṃ vajragīte hrīḥ.
Vomited from the mouth.
Oṃ vajranṛtye aḥ!
She who performs the dance of transformation.
Oṃ vajradhūpe hūṃ.
By means of the application of the vajra-fist, she is the incense ladle.
Oṃ vajrapuṣpe trāṃ.
With a handful of flowers held palm-upward.
Oṃ vajrāloke hrīḥ.
It is bound to a lamp-post.
Oṃ vajragandhe āḥ.
The gesture of the fragrant conch.
Oṃ, for the pervasion of Maitreya, svāhā!
Having formed two vajra-fists, one should join them together evenly;
one should hold them with the index and middle fingers curved in the shape of a flower.
Oṃ, O Infallible One, O You of Infallible Vision, Hūṃ!
Placing the left fist at the hip, one should hold it with the middle and index fingers of the right hand in the shape of an eye.
Oṃ, destroyer of all lower realms, purifier of all lower realms, hūṃ!
[Form the mudrā] with both vajra-fists, the index fingers shaped like hooks.
Oṃ, O you whose intellect destroys all sorrow and darkness, hūṃ!
It is situated on the left hip and has the form of a staff on the right.
Oṃ, to Gandhahastin, hūṃ!
The fist, situated at the navel and shaped like an elephant's trunk, should be held on the right side.
Oṃ, in the Śūraṅgama [samādhi], hūṃ!
Standing on the left hip, she holds a sword with her right hand.
Oṃ, O you who are in the sky, whose eyes are the sky, hūṃ!
Having placed the left fist at the heart, one should rotate the right fist upward.
Oṃ, O Jñānaketu, possessor of wisdom, hūṃ!
With both fists on the right side, she holds a banner.
Oṃ amṛte amṛtavati hūṃ.
One should hold the flask with both hands.
Oṃ, O Moon, O you who gaze like the moon, hūṃ svāhā!
Placing the left fist upon the thigh, one should form the right hand on the right side with the little finger and thumb in the shape of a crescent moon.
Oṃ, O Auspicious One, O Guardian of the Auspicious, hūṃ!
With both hands, one should cause the lotus to blossom.
Oṃ, to Jvālinī, the one of great flames, svāhā!
With both hands, one should place the armor upon the two breasts.
Oṃ vajragarbhe hūṃ.
Having released the middle finger of the right hand, which was resting on the left hip, [he places it] at the heart.
Oṃ, to the inexhaustible, hūṃ, O purifier of inexhaustible karmic obscurations, svāhā!
Placing the left fist at the heart, the right hand should be in the gesture of granting boons.
Oṃ pratibhānavati pratibhānakūṭe hūṃ svāhā!
With his fist placed at the navel of the dwarf, he gives a snap with his right hand.
Oṃ Samantabhadre hūṃ.
Placing the left hand on the hip, the right [hand] forms a jewel-fist.
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa jaḥ!
By forming the hook with the two index fingers and the two little fingers, one becomes Mahāṅkuśī.
Oṃ vajrapāśa hūṃ.
The joint of the upper arm.
Oṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ.
From the two tips of the hips.
Oṃ vajrāveśa hoḥ!
And one should press upon the two backs.
Thus is the action seal (karmamudrā).
Immediately thereafter, visualizing the sattvavajra within one's own heart, one should form the mahāmudrā together with the vajra and vajra-bell.
I am the Vajradhātu.
As it was said by Bodhyagrī:
"I am Vajrasattva.
[He places] his left hand in his lap and his right hand on the ground.
I am Ratnavajra; this very one is the boon-granting [mudrā] of the right hand.
I am Dharmavajra, the supreme samādhi.
I am Vajrakarma;
to her right is Abhaya.
I am Vajrasattva;
with pride, I raise up the vajra;
I am Vajrarāja.
They draw [them] forth with the vajra-hook.
I am Vajrarāga;
having taken up the vajra-arrow.
"I am Vajrasādhu; by employing the word 'Excellent' accompanied by satisfaction, I satisfy all the Tathāgatas."
"I am Vajragarbha;
holding the right vajra-fist at the place of consecration."
I am Vajraprabhā;
by means of the vajra-sun mandala, I illuminate all the Tathāgatas.
"I am the Vajra-staff;
by means of the Cintāmaṇi-banner, one should apply oneself to the perfection of generosity."
I am Vajraprīti,
gladdening with a vajra-smile.
I am Vajranetrā;
holding [a lotus] with her left hand, she displays a blooming lotus with her right hand in a proud manner.
I am Vajrabuddhi;
holding a vajra-sword in my right hand, and a left fist accompanied by a Prajñā manuscript at my heart.
"I am Vajramaṇḍa.
With the middle finger of her right hand, she turns an eight-spoked wheel.
I am Vajravāc;
the vajra-tongues embrace me.
I am the Universal Vajra.
With pride in her left [hand], she holds a double-vajra (viśvavajra) in her right.
I am Vajravīrya.
Wearing the adamantine armor.
"I am Vajracaṇḍā;
placing the weapon of the vajra-fangs in her own mouth, she strikes terror."
I am Vajramuṣṭi;
in the Samayavajramuṣṭi, she presses down upon the five-pronged vajra.
I am Vajralāsyā;
by means of the application of the two types of pride, [she] holds the left hand at the level of the head.
I am Vajramālā;
I am the bearer of the jewel garland.
I am Vajragītā,
playing the lute.
I am Vajranṛtyā;
having formed both hands into the triple-pronged vajra gesture, I dance.
I am Vajradhūpā,
holding an incense burner in my hand.
I am Vajrapuṣpā,
holding a basket of flowers in my hand.
I am Vajrālokā,
holding a torch in her hand.
I am Vajragandhā,
holding a scent-conch in my hand.
I am Maitreya;
with my left hand I hold a water-pot, and with my right I hold a nāga-flower.
I am Amoghadarśī.
With his left hand resting on his hip, he has a lotus in his right eye.
I abandon all states of woe;
my hand holds the goad.
I am Sarvaśokatamonirghātanamati (the one whose intellect destroys all grief and darkness).
With her left hand resting on her hip and holding a staff in her right hand.
I am Gandhahasti;
with my left hip resting [on the ground], I hold a fragrant conch-shell in my right hand.
I am Śūraṅgama;
she stands on my left hip, holding a sword in her right hand.
I am Gaganagañja;
standing on my left hip, he holds a lotus in his right hand containing the treasury of the Dharma.
I am Jñānaketu;
I hold the Cintāmaṇi banner in my right hand, placed upon my left hip.
I am Amṛtaprabha;
I hold a water-jar with my right hand resting upon my left hip;
I am Candraprabha.
I am Bhadrapāla, [visualizing] the right lotus-moon located on the left hip,
and holding a jewel in the right [hand].
I am Jālinīprabhā;
with both hands, I hold a cage.
I am Vajragarbha;
a vajra rests upon an utpala lotus at my left hip, and there is the raising of a vajra at my right heart.
I am Akṣayamati,
holding a flask with both hands.
I am Pratibhānakūṭa;
I rest my left hip upon a lotus bearing a jewel-peak, and make the gesture of snapping the fingers with my right hand.
I am Samantabhadra;
on my left hip is a cluster of jewels, and with my right hand I display the gesture of fearlessness.
I am Vajrāṅkuśa;
my hands hold the goad.
I am Vajrapāśa; I hold a noose in my hand.
I am Vajrasphoṭa;
[this is] the gesture of Vajrasphoṭana.
I am the vajra-possessor;
entry [is achieved] through the application of the bell.
Thus, sealed by the four mudrās, they become bestowers of all accomplishments;
whichever mudrā one should bind for whichever great being.
But in Japan, one should contemplate that entire [world] as being oneself by means of the meaning of the heart.
Thus are the Mahāmudrās.
Therefore,
you should speak with self-restraint.
O Surata, you too should form the mudrā of the Tathāgata family; thereafter,
one should recite the hundred-syllable mantra three times to make it firm.

Oṃ, Vajrasattva, maintain the samaya; abide as Vajrasattva; be firm for me, be pleased with me, be devoted to me; bestow upon me all siddhis; and in all actions, make my mind auspicious. Hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ! O Blessed One, Vajra of all Tathāgatas, do not abandon me; become the Vajra; O Great Samayasattva, Āḥ!
Having taken up the empowerment as before, and having mentally undertaken the vow of the Siddhivajra,
one should then perform the eight outer offerings beginning with the water for the feet (*argha*), as well as the graceful gestures (*lāsya*).
With hands holding a vajra and a vajra-bell, one should perform the lotus-turning gesture.
From the gathering of Vajrasattva, the unsurpassed Vajraratna [arises].
O you who sing the Vajradharma song, become a performer of vajra-activity!
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ!
Thus, uttering this vajra song and performing a dance for each [verse], one should place the bell with pride and recite:
*dharma aḥ*.
The seed-syllable of the bell:
reciting "Oṃ ṭakki hūṃ jaḥ," one should brandish the vajra three times.
Oṃ ṭakki jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ.
Drawing up into the heart:
HŪṂ, the vajra seed-syllable.
The being without beginning or end, Vajrasattva, the Great Joy; Samantabhadra, the soul of all, the pride of the vajra, the refuge, the refuge.
The Blessed One is the supreme primordial person.
The Vajra Reality:
This Blessed One, the supreme Lord of Existence, the sovereign of all that is foremost, the Tathāgata, proclaims the supreme Dharma-samāja:
"Existence is indeed pure by its own nature; it is rendered non-existent by [clinging to] inherent natures."
By means of beings who are pure by nature, the supreme existence is brought about.
The Reality of the Bell.
Thereafter, one should ring the bell in accordance with the Dharma.
Oṃ! Because he is the sign of the arising of space, he is supreme, without beginning or end.
May Vajrasattva—the being composed of the great vajra—grant me success. O supreme of all, the presiding deity of sovereignty, grant me the great siddhi!
May the King who holds all vajras, the supreme syllable, grant me accomplishment.
You are faultless and eternal, the one who inspires passion for all things;
O Blessed One, you are perfected in reality as the Great Passion and the Great Joy. You are internally pure, the pinnacle of all, liberated from the beginning—the Tathāgata.
O Samantabhadra, the Bodhisattva who is the self of all, may we be established in success.

"O supreme among all, through the foremost mudrā of Māheśvarī, may the great accomplishment be perfected for me, O Lord Vajragarbha, by virtue of the great excellence of the Vajra. This is the master’s consecration (ācāryābhiṣeka).
Having thus accomplished oneself in the form of Mahāmudrā and abiding in space, one should contemplate the all-encompassing emptiness;
for the syllable A is the gateway to all phenomena, because they are unproduced from the very beginning.
Through resolute conviction in those objects.
One should resolve with conviction upon the emptiness of all world-systems.
Oṃ, I am pure by nature.

Then, having visualized in the sky a wind mandala arising from the syllable Yaṃ produced by the syllable Hūṃ, a fire mandala arising from Raṃ, a vajra mandala arising from Vaṃ, and a Mahendra mandala arising from Laṃ; above that, a great ocean arising from Buṃ; and in its center, the great Mount Meru arising from Hūṃ-Suṃ-Hūṃ—one should meditate upon it as being square, composed of the four jewels, and adorned with eight peaks.
As before, one should consecrate the ground and so forth as being composed of vajra.
Oṃ vajra-rakṣa, be firm for me; protect all, svāhā!
Oṃ vajrakarma!
Oṃ, by means of the vajra-hūṃkāra, hūṃ!
Oṃ vajrabandha vaṃ.
Oṃ vajrānala hana daha paca maṭha bhañja raṇa hūṃ phaṭ!
With this, one should consecrate the previously mentioned mudrās, such as the enclosure wall and so forth.
Oṃ vajracakre hūṃ!
By means of the vajra-cause action-seal, having emanated a peaked gabled palace consisting of vajra-jewels, lotuses, and various gems at the place of Vairocana:
Āḥ siṃ āḥ!
The lion throne:
*hūṃ gaṃ hūṃ*.
In the place of Akṣobhya is the elephant throne.
Three times, or three times.
