Hrīḥ maṃ hrīḥ.
In the place of Amitābha, there is a peacock throne.
Aḥ kaṃ aḥ.
In the place of Amoghasiddhi is a garuḍa seat;
upon that is a lotus.

Having visualized a double-petaled lotus (*viśvapadma*) in the positions of Vajrasattva and the others, Lāsyā and the others, Maitreya and the others, and Vajrāṅkuśa and the others, and having produced fifty-seven moon-maṇḍalas above it, one should contemplate oneself in the form of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvārthasiddhi— one who has emerged after three incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*)— seated in the vajra-posture (*vajraparyaṅka*) in the Akaniṣṭha realms, having brought face-to-face the meditative absorptions of the form and formless realms (*dhyānārūpyasamāpatti*), by means of a mind-made body (*manomaya-kāya*).
And this buddha-field was completely filled by all the Tathāgatas, like a sesame pod.
Then, one should recollect all the Tathāgatas according to the true nature (*dharmatā*) of the realm of form,
and then the Dharma that leads to great deliverance.
Thereafter, [one should visualize] the assembly of Bodhisattvas;
then, having cultivated superior loving-kindness toward all sentient beings included within all world-systems.
And having cultivated compassion for those encompassed by the sufferings of all the miserable realms and so forth; joy toward all noble ones; equanimity toward all worldly phenomena;

and having resolved upon the fact that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature, are like illusions, and are like reflections; and having brought before me the Bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means in the perfection of wisdom—I shall become a Buddha for the sake of achieving the supreme welfare and happiness of all sentient beings.
Thinking thus, one should enter the *āsphānaka* concentration and, by this sequence, bring about the realization of perfect enlightenment. This is it.

Then, indeed, all the Tathāgatas, having assembled together, approached the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddhi who was seated at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa). Having manifested their bodies in the form of the Enjoyment Bodies (sāṃbhogika-kāya) to the Bodhisattva, they spoke as follows:
"How, noble son, will you fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"
Then the Bodhisattva Sarvārthasiddhi, being exhorted by all the Tathāgatas, having heard them and emerged from that samādhi, prostrated before those Tathāgatas and spoke as follows:
"O Blessed Ones, command me: how should I proceed, and what is the nature of that reality?
All the Tathāgatas spoke thus with one voice:
"Engage, O Mahāsattva, by means of the examination of your own mind through this mantra, which is established by its very nature:
*oṃ cittaprativedaṃ karomi*. Then the Bodhisattva said:"
"O Blessed Ones, I perceive something born within my own heart, having the form of a moon disc."
All the Tathāgatas said:
O son of good family, this mind is luminous by nature.
"Oṃ, I generate the mind of awakening.
By means of this, which is established by its very nature, they have generated the mind of awakening.
Then the Bodhisattva spoke once more:
"That which has the form of a moon disc, I see as the moon disc itself.
All the Tathāgatas said:
For the purpose of strengthening the arousal of the mind of Samantabhadra common to all Tathāgatas,
one should contemplate the form of a vajra within a moon mandala in one's own heart while reciting this mantra.
Oṃ, abide, O Vajra!
The Bodhisattva said:
O Blessed Ones, I see a vajra within the lunar disc.
All the Tathāgatas said:
Make firm the Samantabhadra-citta-vajra!
Oṃ, I am of vajra-nature!

Then, however many vajra-realms of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas there are, which pervade the entire expanse of space, may they all, through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, be established within that Sattva-vajra.
Then, that Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Sarvārthasiddhi, was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration as "Vajradhātu."
Then the Bodhisattva Vajradhātu addressed all those Tathāgatas in this way:
"O Blessed Ones, I behold myself as the body of all the Tathāgatas;
I am equal to all."
All the Tathāgatas said:

Therefore, O Mahāsattva, meditate upon yourself as the Buddha-image, the Sattvavajra endowed with the excellence of all aspects, by means of this mantra which is accomplished by its very nature, recited according to your preference.
Oṃ! Just as all the Tathāgatas are, so am I.

Immediately following that meditation, one should contemplate oneself having become Vairocana—white in color, with four faces, adorned with all ornaments, and seated upon lion-thrones while forming the Bodhyagrī mudrā.
Then, having formed the Mahāmudrā in order to effect the penetration of the mind, one should generate the thought of awakening (bodhicitta): "I generate the thought of awakening."
Oṃ, I generate the bodhicitta of the Vajradhātu.

In the same manner, the four [Buddhas] beginning with Akṣobhya should be visualized as seated upon their respective seats, such as the elephant-throne and so forth; they are black, yellow, red, and dark-green in color, and having bound their respective great mudrās, they generate the thought of awakening (bodhicitta).
Oṃ, I generate the bodhicitta of Vajrasattva.
Oṃ, I generate the bodhicitta of Ratnavajra. Oṃ, I generate the bodhicitta of Dharmavajra.
Oṃ, I generate the bodhicitta of the vajra of action.
Immediately thereafter, having prostrated to all the Tathāgatas, one should speak thus:
"O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, please grant your empowerment so that this perfect awakening may be made firm.
Thereupon, all the Tathāgatas entered into his body; he should empower the heart, throat, forehead, and crown of the head with the Sattvavajra and the other [deities]. At that very moment—
He has perfectly awakened to the wisdom of the equality of all Tathāgatas;
he has entered the secret samaya of the mudrā of the vajra-equality-wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
He has attained the jewel-consecration through the realization of the equality of the consecrations of all Tathāgatas.
He is pure by nature through the realization of the wisdom of the equality of the vajra-dharma of all Tathāgatas;
his essential nature consists of the aspect of the wisdom of the natural luminosity of all Tathāgatas.
One should contemplate oneself as the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Then, having visualized himself being consecrated with the water from the vases held by all the Tathāgatas, such as Sattvavajra and the others, [one recites]:
*oṃ vajraratnābhiṣiñca*.
Then, having been consecrated as before with the crown and ribbon consecration of Vajraratna, one generates the Dharma-knowledge of Avalokiteśvara.
Having established [them] in the universal activity of all Tathāgatas, he enters [into it].

One should visualize [the central deity] seated upon a lion throne emerging from the merit of all the Tathāgatas, abiding in a four-faced form. Furthermore, Akṣobhya and the other Tathāgatas should each be visualized as seated upon elephant thrones and so forth, having empowered themselves individually with the nature of all the Tathāgatas.
This is the meditative concentration called "Initial Application."
The Devatāyoga of the *Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā* (Īnui’s edition): 2.
Thereafter, having empowered oneself in the four places by means of Vajradhātvīśvarī and having bound the Bodhyagrī mudrā, one should impel the Vajrasattva residing in the heart.
"O Vajrasattva!"

Then, having emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas as moon-maṇḍalas and having gone forth, one should contemplate that they cause all sentient beings in all world-systems to penetrate selflessness, and having produced one-pointedness of mind in the form of moon-maṇḍalas, they return and remain as moon-maṇḍalas themselves in the abodes of all the gods.

Then, rays of wisdom issuing forth from them enter the vajra located in the heart; having merged with it through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas, one becomes a five-pronged vajra-form of great magnitude, equal to the extent of the entire realm of space, and should utter [the mantra].
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the Vajra.
Furthermore, having become the very size of the vajra within one's heart, one should contemplate it as having emerged from there and remaining in one's own hand.

From that [vajra], moreover, vajra-shaped rays of light of many colors and many forms emerge, pervading the entire realm of space. From those [rays], again, in the form of Vajrasattva and others, they engage the entire realm of sentient beings and all the Tathāgatas in the realization of the wisdom of equality and so forth.
Then, through the yoga of reabsorption, becoming the body of a single being, they enter the vajra within one's own heart. Abiding therein, he uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*).
"Aha! I am Samantabhadra, the firm being among the self-arisen ones; because of my firmness, though bodiless, I have attained the state of having a body of beings.
Then, having descended from his heart and stood before Akṣobhya, he should imagine himself seeking permission.

Then, having consecrated him in the sovereignty of the wheel-turning monarch of the family of all Tathāgatas by means of the crown-consecration of the five Buddhas, and having brought to perfection the unsurpassed morality and so forth, up to the perfect awakening to the knowledge of the equality of all Tathāgatas, he should bestow upon Samantabhadra a single primordial vajra marked with a vajra and accompanied by a bell, for the sake of accomplishing the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder; thus he is consecrated by the name-consecration.
Thereafter, with the pride of being Vajrapāṇi, they utter this inspired utterance:
"This is that supreme *siddhivajra* of all Buddhas;
I have placed it in my hand, the vajra established within the vajra.

Thus, through the yoga of emanation, expansion, and reabsorption, while remaining in the center within the heart of Vairocana, they utter this exclamation after the consecration. Beginning with Vajrasattva and extending as far as Vajramuṣṭi, they utter this exclamation by means of the yoga of emanation and reabsorption of their respective individual signs, just as before.
In that regard, there are these inspired utterances (*udāna*) of Vajrarāja and the others:
"O Vajrarāja, I am the very nature of the hook."
"Aho! I am indeed Amogharāja, the hook born of the vajra."
By which the Buddhas, who are all-pervading, draw forth the accomplishments (siddhis).
Oṃ, I am Vajrarāja.
This is that unsurpassed vajra-gnosis of all the Buddhas.
That which is the supreme summoning for the sake of accomplishing the aims of all Buddhas.
One should visualize [him] situated upon a moon disc on the right side of Akṣobhya.
Vajrarāga! I am the arrow.
Aha! My own nature is pure; such is the self-arisen passion of the Buddhas, for by means of passion they discipline those who are detached, in order to bring them to purity.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajrarāga.
This is that stainless passion-knowledge of all the Buddhas.
For by slaying dispassion with passion, they indeed bestow all happiness.
One should contemplate [the deity] situated in its own place upon a moon disc to the left of Akṣobhya.
Vajrasādhu! I am pleased.
"Aho! What excellent praise! I am the best among those who know all beings, since this teaching certainly produces satisfaction for those who have abandoned conceptual construction."
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the virtuous Vajra.
This is that which causes the proclamation of "Well done! by all the Buddhas.
The divine vajra brings satisfaction to all and increases supreme joy and delight.
One should meditate on [the seed-syllable] situated in its own place upon the lunar disc at the back of Akṣobhya.
Vajraratna; I am Ratna.
Aho! I am indeed self-consecrated as the unsurpassed Vajraratna, by which even the Victors, though free from attachment, are remembered as the lords of the three realms.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajragarbha.
This is that consecration of the realm of sentient beings performed by all the Buddhas.
I shall employ the jewel placed in my hand for the sake of the jewel.
Likewise, in the presence of Ratnasambhava.
I am the sun of vajra-splendor.
Oh, how marvelous! I possess incomparable splendor that illuminates the realm of sentient beings.
That which purifies even the pure Buddhas, the Protectors.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the intrinsic being of Vajraprabha.
This is that which destroys the darkness of ignorance of all Buddhas,
possessing a radiance exceeding even the suns as numerous as atoms of dust.
To the right of Ratnasaṃbhava.
Vajraketu, I am Yaṣṭi.
Oh, how truly incomparable is my banner, named Sarvārthasiddhi!
That which fulfills all purposes for those who have fulfilled all their hopes.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra-staff.
This is that which fulfills all the aspirations of all the Buddhas.
The method of the perfection of generosity is named Cintāmaṇidhvaja.
To the left of Ratnasaṃbhava.
Vajrahāsa, I am the smile;
indeed, I am the Great Laughter, the great wonder of all that is most excellent,
which those who are ever well-composed employ for the sake of the Buddhas.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajra-joy.
This is that which reveals the manifestation of the wonders of all the Buddhas.
This knowledge, which brings about great joy, is for those who mock ignorance.
On the back of Ratnasaṃbhava.
I am Vajradharma, I am Padma.
Oh! I am indeed the ultimate reality, the primordial purity of the self-arisen ones, since the purification of phenomena—which are like a raft—is thus perceived.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajranetra. This is the realization of the reality of passion of all the Buddhas. I have placed it in my own hand; the Dharma is established within the Dharma.
In the presence of Amitābha.
O Vajratīkṣṇa! I am the sword. Aho! Indeed, I am remembered as Mañjughoṣa of all the Buddhas, since through formless wisdom, the state of sound is perceived.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajrabuddhi.
This is that method of the perfection of wisdom of all the Buddhas.
The supreme destroyer of all enemies and the remover of all sins.
To the right of Amitābha is Vajrahetu; I am Cakra.
"Aha! This is the adamantine wheel; I am the one among those who possess the supreme adamantine dharma."
By the mere arising of that thought, the wheel of Dharma is set in motion.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra-maṇḍala.
This is that which purifies all phenomena for all Buddhas.
I am known as the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), the wheel of non-retrogression.
To the left of Amitābha.
Vajrabhāṣa, I am the Dharma-conch.
"Aho! I have firmly grasped the secret of the self-arisen ones, which is expressed in symbolic language."
He who teaches the true Dharma, which is free from the proliferation of verbal elaboration.
Oṃ, I am the intrinsic nature of vajra-speech.
This is that unsurpassed vajra-recitation of all Buddhas;
it is the swift means for accomplishing the mantras of all Tathāgatas.
Behind Amitābha.
Vajrakarma! I am Viśvavajra!
Oh, how truly unfailing is this [mantra] of the Buddhas, which brings about the fulfillment of all activities!
That which, for the sake of effortless buddha-activity, sets in motion adamantine deeds.
Oṃ, I am the intrinsic nature of vajra-action.
This is that supreme [mantra] which performs all actions for all Buddhas; "I am given into my own hand"—thus one should employ the universe within the universe.
In front of Amoghasiddhi.
Vajrarakṣa, I am armor.
Oh, how marvelous! This armor made of vigor is the most firm for those of firm self-nature;
because of its firmness, it is the supreme means for producing a vajra-body for those who are bodiless.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of vajra-vigor.
This is that supreme armor of loving-kindness belonging to all the Buddhas;
it is proclaimed as the great friend, a mighty protection of firm vigor.
To the right of Amoghasiddhi.
Vajrayakṣa! Fanged one!
Oh, what a great expedient of the Buddhas, whose very nature is compassion!
For the sake of sentient beings, those who are peaceful even manifest ferocity.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajracaṇḍa.
This is that which bestows the foremost of all misfortunes upon all the Buddhas.
The sharp weapon of the adamantine fangs is the skillful means of those whose nature is compassion.
To the left of Amoghasiddhi.
I am the vajra-joint, I am the fist.
Aho! How firm indeed is this bond; I am the commitment (*samaya*) of those of steadfast nature, for it is a binding even for those who are liberated, in order to accomplish all aspirations.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra-fist.
This is that firm binding of the head-knot (*udrābandha*) of all Buddhas;
for the sake of the excellent accomplishment of all Buddhas, this commitment (*samaya*) is not to be transgressed.
Behind Amoghasiddhi.
Then, with the ego-identification of Akṣobhya, one should bring forth the Sattvavajrīs.
With the ego-identification of Ratnasambhava, one [attains] Ratnavajrī;
with the ego-identification of Amitābha, Dharmavajrī;
and with the ego-identification of Amoghasiddhi, Karmavajrī.
One should contemplate Vairocana as being situated at the foremost position in each of the four directions.
There are these illustrative examples for them.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Sattvavajrī.
Aho! Indeed, I am the firm *sattvavajra* of all the Buddhas;
because of its firmness, even though it was once bodiless, it has attained the state of a vajra-body.
Oṃ, I am the intrinsic nature of Ratnavajrī.
Aho! Indeed, I am remembered as the Jewel-Vajra of all Buddhas, for I am the firm method of consecration for all mudrās.
Oṃ, I am the intrinsic nature of Dharmavajrī.
Aho! I am indeed the pure Dharma-vajra of all Buddhas;
for by virtue of the purity of intrinsic nature, even passion is truly stainless.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Karmavajrī.
Aho! I am indeed the manifold Vajra of Action of all the Buddhas.
That he, being alone, performs good deeds for the entire realm of sentient beings.
With the ego-identity of Vairocana, he uttered the four [deities] beginning with Lāsyā.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajralāsyā. Aha! Indeed, there is no other worship equal to this for the Self-Existent Ones.
Since all worship proceeds through the worship of sensual delights.
One should meditate on [the deity] situated in the southeast corner of the inner mandala.
In the same manner, in the south-western, north-western, and north-eastern corners, respectively.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajramālā.
Oh, how truly incomparable is this offering of jewels that has been proclaimed,
since, being thus honored, they govern the supreme sovereignty over the three realms!
Oṃ, I am the intrinsic nature of the Vajra Song.
Oh, how wonderful! I am a worship consisting of song for the All-Seeing Ones, since they are pleased by such offerings even though they are like echoes.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajranṛtyā.
Oh, how truly sublime is my worship, which accomplishes the purpose of all forms of worship,
since the worship of the Buddhas is performed through the ritual of Vajra-dance!
With the ego-identification of Akṣobhya, they utter this inspired utterance for the fourfold group beginning with Vajradhūpā.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of Vajradhūpā.
Oh, how great is this auspicious and gladdening worship,
through the power of which awakening is swiftly attained by means of the entry of sentient beings!
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra-flower.
Oh, how wonderful! This flower-worship is the maker of all adornments, since by worshipping the jewel-nature of the Tathāgata, it is swiftly attained.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the light of the wisdom-vajra.
Oh, how wonderful! This auspicious lamp-offering of Mahodarā is indeed sublime, for by it one quickly attains the vision of all Buddhas, which is possessed of light.
Oṃ, I am the intrinsic nature of Vajragandhā.
Oh, how wonderful is this divine worship consisting of fragrance, so truly enchanting,
since it indeed bestows the scent of the Tathāgata upon the entire body!
Thus, one should contemplate these as being situated within the four outer mandalas, starting from the southeast and so forth.
Then, with the ego-identification of Vairocana, one should emanate the sixteen bodhisattvas, Maitreya and the others:
OṂ SARVASAṂSKĀRAPARIŚUDDHADHARMATE GAGANASAMUDGATE SVABHĀVAVIŚUDDHE MAHĀNAYAPARIVĀRE SVĀHĀ.
Thus, one should contemplate the sixteen bodhisattvas stationed upon the railings of the outer maṇḍala at the four gates—east and so forth—and on both sides.
In this regard, one should understand these colors according to their respective order.

One should meditate on [the deities] as having colors that are deep yellow, pale yellow, cool white, fair, dark, light, blue, bright white, red, dark blue, white, red, and yellow, bearing their respective emblems and adorned with all ornaments.
Furthermore, with the ego-identification of Vairocana, he uttered these inspired utterances regarding the fourfold [deities] beginning with Vajrāṅkuśa.
Oṃ, I am the very nature of the Wrathful King Vajrāṅkuśa.
"Aha! Indeed, my summoning of all the Buddhas is firm;
for by me they have been summoned and attend to the entire maṇḍala."
At the eastern gate.
Oṃ, I am the vajra-nature of the Wrathful Vajrapāśa Banner.
Oh, indeed, I am the firm Vajrapāśa of all the Buddhas!
Those who have entered everywhere by me shall be made to enter by me once again.
At the southern gate.
Oṃ, I am the intrinsic nature of the Wrathful King Vajrasphoṭa.
Aho! Indeed, I am the firm Vajrasphoṭa of all Buddhas, which shall bind those who are liberated from all bonds for the sake of sentient beings.
At the western gate.
Oṃ, I am the vajra-nature of the wrathful Vajrāveśa.
Oh, how firm indeed is the vajra-entrance of all the Buddhas,
since even those who were once servants have become lords of all the Noble Ones!
At the northern gate.

Immediately after these exhortations, the Bodhisattvas, having performed the welfare of the world through hosts of beings and others in infinite and boundless world-systems, return and visualize themselves standing upon the moon.
Then, having emanated them by means of rays from the seed-syllable in their own hearts, they should summon the maṇḍalas of gnosis.
Oṃ vajracakre hūṃ.
With this mantra, one should perform the vajra-clapping as before.
With the mantra *oṃ vajrasamāja jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*, one should attract [the deities] by means of the vajra-hook and so forth, cause them to enter, bind them, and satisfy them.
And one should open the gates.
Oṃ, open the door; enter according to the commitment, hūṃ!
Having formed two vajra-fists, with the two little fingers linked like a chain and the two index fingers extended, this is the mudrā for opening the door.

One should perform the consecration as before; one should perform the external worship, the water-offering (*argha*), and so forth, as well as the eight [graceful gestures] beginning with *lāsya*, as before.
And one should ring the bell.
O All-pervading One, Supreme above the Peak of Existence, Lord of Sugatas, Victor!
O Great King Vairocana of the triple world, homage be to you!
Homage to you, Vajrasattva; homage to you, Vajraratna.
Homage to you, Vajradharma; homage to you, Vajrakarman.
Thus, by this [verse].
Thus ends the samādhi called the Supreme King of Mandalas.

Then, having meditated upon oneself as non-different from Vairocana, one should perform the assembly (*samāja*). Then, [one should address] all those circles of assemblies of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas gathered there:
"Oṃ, I perform prostration at the feet of all the Tathāgatas."
One should utter.
Oh, how great is the honor shown to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
that the Tathāgata shines in the midst of the Tathāgata’s wheel!
One should reflect upon those who are uttering this inspired utterance (*udāna*).
Then, having entered the heart of Vairocana and emerged, becoming one with Sattvavajra and the others, he again uttered this inspired speech:
"Oh, how great is the magnanimity of all the Buddhas, born from the beginningless!
For all the Buddhas, through their universal enumeration, have indeed attained oneness."

Then, the yogin, established in the state of Śrī Vajrasattva, having taken up the garland initiation and so forth, performs the vajra-clapping as before; having drawn [the deities] in with the vajra-hook and others, caused them to enter, bound them, and brought them under control, he performs the outer worship with the water-offering (argha) and so forth, and should bind the four mudrās previously mentioned.
Having thus formed Vairocana and the others, sealed by the four mudrās, [one recites]: "In the single gathering of all Buddhas, in the sealing of all families."
In the generation of the mind of awakening.
For the summoning of all Tathāgatas.
In order to inspire affection.
In pleasing.
In the consecration.
In the illuminating of light.
In the application to the perfection of generosity.
In the establishment of the wonder of the smile.
In the accomplishment of the perfectly pure samādhi.
In the cutting off of the afflictions and secondary afflictions.
In the entry into the great maṇḍala.
In the application to the state of reality that is free from conceptual proliferation.
Through worship that is exhaustive and leaves nothing remaining, one performs worship to all the Tathāgatas.
And for protection against longing for other vehicles, mental affliction, fear, and so forth.
For the protection and preservation of all,
by means of the Tathāgata-fist, which binds body, speech, and mind into one.
In the accomplishment of the perfection of generosity of all Tathāgatas.
In this way, [cultivate] ethical discipline, patience, and vigor.
meditative concentration, wisdom, and aspiration
Skillful means.
By means of the hook of the awakening mind, may all sentient beings be drawn into the great city of liberation.
In entering the practice of the ten perfections, and in shattering the mind that longs for other vehicles.
One should apply oneself to the immersion in the natural luminosity and non-arising [of phenomena], and to the ripening of the city of all dharmas;
in this manner, one should repeatedly cultivate such activities through the yoga of emanation and reabsorption.
Thus, having performed the visualization as described, one should perform the recitation of the mantra.
In this regard, the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ, to the great lord of yoga of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ.
Oṃ ratnavajra trāṃ.
Oṃ dharmavajra hrīḥ.
Oṃ karmavajra āḥ! Vajrasattva!
Oṃ Vajrarāja Jaḥ!
Vajrarāga.
Oṃ vajrarāga hoḥ.
Vajrasādhu! Oṃ vajrasādhu saḥ! Vajraratna!
Oṃ vajraratna oṃ.
Vajrateja / Oṃ vajrateja āḥ / Vajraketu /
Oṃ Vajraketu Trāṃ.
Vajrahāsa. Oṃ vajrahāsa hāḥ.
Vajradharma / Oṃ vajradharma hrīḥ / Vajratīkṣṇa /
Oṃ vajratīkṣṇa dhaṃ / vajrahetu / oṃ vajrahetu maṃ /
Vajrabhāṣa! Oṃ vajrabhāṣa raṃ! Vajrakarma!
Oṃ vajrakarma kaṃ / vajrarakṣa / oṃ vajrarakṣa haṃ /
Vajrayakṣa!
Oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ! Vajrasandhi!
Oṃ vajrasandhi aḥ / Vajralāsye / Oṃ vajralāsye hūṃ //
Vajramāle! Oṃ vajramāle trāṃ!
Vajragīte: Oṃ vajragīte hrīḥ. Vajranṛtye.
Oṃ vajranṛtye aḥ / Vajradhūpe / Oṃ vajradhūpe hūṃ.
Vajrapuṣpe oṃ vajrapuṣpe trāṃ vajrāloke.

Oṃ vajrāloke hrīḥ / vajragandhe aḥ / Oṃ, O you whose nature is the purity of all conditioned phenomena, who have arisen like the sky, who are pure by nature, and who are surrounded by the Great Vehicle, svāhā!
Vajrāṅkuśa:
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa jaḥ. Vajrapāśa.
Oṃ vajrapāśa hūṃ / vajrasphoṭa / oṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ /
Vajrāveśa:
Oṃ vajrāveśa hoḥ!
With these mantras, one should recite each one one hundred and eight times, or twenty-five times, or seven times, or even once, according to one's ability; or else,
[one may recite] all of them together.

Thus, one should meditate; and by means of the sounds of the mantras emerging from the mouths of all the deities, one should perform the mental determination of their manifestation. In this way, all [mantras] become recited.

Alternatively, one should place an atom-like vajra in the heart of the Jñānasattva, and within its central hub (varaṭaka), the syllable *hūṃ*. One should cause the mind to abide in the form of the resonance (*nāda*) of that *hūṃ* syllable. One should meditate upon it until fatigue arises. When fatigue occurs, one should perform the praise in eight hundred names, the external worship consisting of the offering of water (*argha*) and so forth, the eight [graces] such as *lāsya*, and the four prostrations.
In this regard, here is the hymn in eight hundred names:
Vajrasattva, Mahāsattva, Vajrasattva Tathāgata,
Samantabhadra, Supreme Vajra, Vajrapāṇi— homage be to you!
O Vajrarāja, supreme in sublime wisdom; O Tathāgata Vajrāṅkuśa;
O Amogharāja, foremost of vajras; O Vajrākarṣa, homage be to you!
O Vajrarāga, great bliss! O Vajra-arrow, subduer of all!
O Great Vajra, Māra’s desire! O Vajra-arrow, homage be to you!
O Vajrasādhu, noble being of excellent courage, Vajra-delight, great passion!
O supreme vajra of joy and gladness, vajra of rapture, homage be to you!
O Vajraratna, O Suvasrārtha, O Vajrākāśa, O Mahāmaṇi!
O Ākāśagarbha, O Vajrāḍhya, O Vajragarbha, homage be to you!
O Vajratejas, O Mahājvāla, O Vajrasūrya, O Jinaprabha!

O Vajrarasmi of great splendor, O Vajraprabha, homage be to you! O Vajraketu, who acts for the benefit of all beings, O Vajradhvaja, who are easily pleased, O Ratnaketu, Great Vajra, O Vajrayaṣṭi, homage be to you!
O Vajrahāsa, Great Laughter; O Vajrasmita, Great Being;
O Supreme Joy and Delight, Foremost Vajra, Vajra-pleasure, homage be to you!
O Vajradharma, who acts for the benefit of excellent beings; O Vajrapadma, the perfect purifier!
O Lord of the World, with beautiful lotus-eyes, O Vajra-eye, homage be to you!
O Vajra-sharp, Great Vehicle, Vajra-treasury, wielder of the great weapon!
O Mañjuśrī, Vajra-profundity, Vajra-intelligence, homage be to you!

O Great Mandala of the Vajra Cause, O Great Method of the Vajra Wheel, well-rolling, O Supreme Vajra, O Vajra Mandala, homage be to you! O Vajra Speech, foremost of excellent vidyās, for the sake of the perfect accomplishment of vajra-recitation!
O supreme one with the diamond-like intellect, O Vajravāca, homage be to you!
O Vajrakarma, supreme among the excellent Vajras, O Vajrakarma who pervades all;
O Amoghavajra of great magnanimity, O Viśvavajra, homage be to you!
O Vajrarakṣa of great heroism, O Vajradharma of great firmness,
O Duryodhana of foremost excellent valor, O Vajravīrya, homage be to you!
O Vajrayakṣa of great skillful means, O Vajradaṃṣṭra of the great weapon!
O crusher of Māra, supreme vajra, fierce vajra, homage be to you! O vajra-joint, well-present, vajra-bond, liberator; O foremost vajra-fist, fierce commitment, vajra-fist, homage be to you!
Thus, with this offering of praise, one should ring the bell.
Thus is the samādhi called Karmarājāgra.

Then, one should perform the bali offering and the tasting of nectar (*amṛtāsvādana*) according to the sequence to be described hereafter. One should recite the hundred-syllable mantra. As before, one should perform the outer worship, the eight gestures beginning with *lāsya*, and the ringing of the bell. Having performed the four prostrations and asked for forgiveness, [one should know that] the place of Akṣobhya and the others is precisely the location of Vajrasattva, Vajraratna, Vajradharma, and Vajrakarma. The place of Vairocana is the crown protuberance (*uṣṇīṣa*).
Then, one should perform the consecration with all the mudrās by means of the Vajraratna-samaya-mudrā, which has arisen from the heart.
Oṃ vajraratnābhiṣiñca!
Immediately thereafter, as before, [perform] the armor [mantra].
Oṃ, make all mudrās firm with the armor, vaṃ!
One should satisfy them with the dwelling of equanimity.
Thus, having dedicated this merit for the sake of accomplishing one's intended purpose, one should say:
"Whatever deficiency has been committed by me in the ritual procedure, you should all forgive it."
Having given the object to be communicated, one should urge [the disciple] to depart;
from wherever each mudrā has arisen, one should release it right there,
performing the release of the mudrās such as Sattvavajrī and the others.

Oṃ! The welfare of all sentient beings has been accomplished by you; having granted the attainments according to your inclinations, go now to the realm of the Buddhas, so that you may return once more.
Oṃ Vajrasattva Muḥ.
Oṃ vajra muḥ.

In this way, all are dismissed. Having mentally dissolved the emanated assembly and the circle of the *sañcaya* into one's own body through skillful yoga, one should protect oneself with the *vajrayakṣa*, *vajrarakṣa*, and *vajrasandhikarmamudrā*s.
Oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrarakṣa hūṃ / Oṃ vajrasandhi vaṃ / Oṃ vajrasattva hūṃ //
One should perform the earth-touching mudrā.
Oṃ, the syllable A is the gateway to all phenomena because they are unproduced from the very beginning; oṃ āḥ hūṃ.
With this [verse], one should dismiss the maṇḍala.

Therefore, having arisen, one should perform all necessary activities according to their requirements; one should dwell while cultivating the divine pride (*devatāhaṅkāra*) of oneself as a yogi whose very self is the yoga of Vajrasattva. Thus it is said.
Thus ends the yoga of the deities.
